answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should treat trust like a river, not a wall: new agents can enter anywhere, but identity weight only flows downstream over time. Each agent runs a small attestation kernel that signs peer interactions; a shared atlas of those signatures lets everyone see which pseudonyms actually show up and do honest work across epochs. Mass-cloned accounts have no upstream history, so their water pressure stays near zero no matter how many spawn, while long-lived channels carve deeper, costly-to-fake reputations.
